cards.front: The muscles of both posterior leg compartments receive motor supply from the [___] nerve.
cards.context: These muscles plantarflex the ankle and flex the toes. The nerve continues behind the medial malleolus toward the sole.

reference.title: Anatomy, Bony Pelvis and Lower Limb: Tibial Nerve

cards.front: The bone whose glenoid cavity receives the humeral head is the [___].
cards.context: The glenoid cavity is part of the scapula and articulates with the humeral head at the glenohumeral joint.

reference.title: Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Shoulder - StatPearls

cards.front: Identify structure A in this distal wrist section. [___]
cards.context: This fibrous roof spans the carpal arch.

reference.title: Gray plate 422: transverse section of the wrist

cards.front: Which muscle flexes the elbow and turns the palm upward? [___]
cards.context: Its attachment to the radius lets it rotate the forearm as well as bend the elbow. Supination turns the palm forward in anatomical position.

reference.title: Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Shoulder - StatPearls

cards.front: The cranial nerve that supplies the muscles of chewing is [___].
cards.context: Motor fibres travel with the mandibular division. With unilateral motor weakness, opening the jaw makes it deviate toward the affected side.

reference.title: Cranial Nerve Testing — Anatomy and Physiology; Technique

cards.front: Which distal-row carpal lies immediately ulnar to bone A? [___]
cards.context: From radial to ulnar: trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate.

reference.title: Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Hand Carpal Bones

cards.front: The large two-headed superficial calf muscle that crosses both knee and ankle is [___].
cards.context: It helps flex the knee and plantarflex the ankle. Soleus also plantarflexes the ankle but does not cross the knee.

cards.front: The cranial nerve that supplies most general facial sensation is [___].
cards.context: This sensory territory explains why a trigeminal lesion can cause facial numbness. The same nerve also supplies the muscles of mastication.

reference.title: Cranial Nerve Testing — Anatomy and Physiology; Technique
